I am Toru Muranishi, who had an appointment with you today.

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

examples.text: 誠意の表れですよ、安いもんです。
examples.trans: It's an expression of sincerity—a small price to pay.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Opposite of 裏 (hidden side); also means 'outside/front'.

examples.text: 人間には表と裏がある。
examples.trans: Human beings have a public face and a hidden side.
Go outside / come into the open.

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.
Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

examples.text: 皆さんいいですか？カメラに向かって最高の笑顔でいきますよ。
examples.trans: Is everyone ready? Face the cameras and give your very best smiles.

examples.text: お世話になっております。今ちょうど向かっていますよ。
examples.trans: Thank you for everything. We are on our way right now.

examples.text: リムジン八台に女優、男優、助監督を乗せてスタート地点へ向かう。
examples.trans: Eight limousines carrying actresses, actors, and assistant directors will head to the starting line.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: どうぞ、おひとついかがですか？取れたての巨峰でございます。
examples.trans: Here, won't you try one? They are freshly picked Kyoho grapes.

examples.text: 社員の皆様とおいしくね、巨峰を頂いておりますよ。
examples.trans: I am enjoying delicious Kyoho grapes here with all your employees.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Verbal noun; 約束する means 'to promise'.

examples.text: 約束の時間に遅れました。
examples.trans: I was late for the appointment time.

meanings.note: Polite/honorific plural pronoun for addressing an audience or group.

examples.text: 皆様のご健康をお祈りします。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 今ね、御社の社長が何をしてるかご存じですか？
examples.trans: Do you all know what your company's president is doing right now?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

examples.text: 近い将来爆発的に普及する衛星放送についてご存じですか？
examples.trans: Have you heard of satellite broadcasting, which will soon spread explosively?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.en: and so; because of that; with that
meanings.note: Conjunction indicating a result or asking 'and then what happened?'.

examples.text: それでどうなりましたか。
それで問題が解決しました。
examples.trans: With that, the problem was solved.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

examples.text: それでそんな幼稚なことしてるのか？
examples.trans: And that's why he's pulling something so childish?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Conjunctive particle giving a reason, softer than から.

examples.text: 雨が降っているので、家にいます。
examples.trans: Since it's raining, I'm staying home.

examples.text: 時間がないので急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: We don't have time, so let's hurry.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: そうです。この巨大アンテナから飛んだ電波を衛星がキャッチするんです。
examples.trans: That's right. Orbiting satellites catch the waves beamed from these giant antennas.

examples.text: そして今度は衛星から地球に電波が降り注ぐ。
examples.trans: And then the signals shower back down from the satellite onto the earth.

examples.text: もちろん。そのための衛星だ。
examples.trans: Of course. That is what the satellite is for.

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Standard polite 'goodbye'.
